misconceptions.description: Entering student names, grades, or identifiable details into a public AI tool to get help
misconceptions.trigger: teacher or student pastes a named student's record or work into a consumer chatbot
misconceptions.feedback: Strip identifiers before prompting. Public tools may store and train on inputs, so describe the situation without names, IDs, or other personally identifiable information.

misconceptions.description: Believing a short vague prompt is fine because the model will fill in the right intent
misconceptions.trigger: student submits a one-line prompt and accepts whatever generic output returns
misconceptions.feedback: Model how to specify audience, purpose, grade level, and constraints in the prompt. Responsible prompting is a teachable skill, not a guess the model corrects.

misconceptions.description: Teaching students to copy the first AI response rather than evaluate and iterate on it
misconceptions.trigger: students paste the first output as their final answer without checking it
misconceptions.feedback: Build an iterate-and-verify routine: read the output critically, check it against a source, and refine the prompt. The first response is a draft, not the answer.

misconceptions.description: Assigning open-ended chatbot use without considering students' age, consent, and developmental readiness
misconceptions.trigger: teacher gives young students unsupervised access to a general-purpose chatbot
misconceptions.feedback: Match the prompting activity to age and policy: check terms-of-service minimum ages, supervision needs, and content risk before letting students prompt freely.
